newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN BOND YIELDS OFF AHEAD OF MAJOR TEST.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BOND YIELDS OFF AHEAD OF MAJOR TEST.

text.p: *Australian bond yields softened in early trading in anticipation of a sluggish July labour force report at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
*U.S. Treasuries steady ahead of 30-year bond auction.

Australian bond yields softened in early trading in anticipation of a sluggish July labour force report at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) and what could prove to be the market's first major test after last week's official rate cut.

Median forecasts centre on a 25,000 employment rise after the modest 11,900 increase in June, although it would need an outcome of over 60,000 to show any real improvement in the labour market, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
The median expectation for the unemployment rate is 8.6 percent versus 8.5 percent previously.

The reaction to the data is expected to be more notable at the short end, and particularly bill futures, given that the labour market has been one of the key factors behind the five rate cuts seen seen so far this cycle.

September and December bill futures have been trading at a discount to the new official 5.0 percent cash rate since the Reserve Bank eased policy last Wednesday as the market has yet to completely rule out a sixth easing.
Meanwhile, the Australian Treasury said late on Wednesday that it had no plans to change its borrowing needs for 1997/98, keeping projected fixed coupon issuance at A$5.0/6.0 billion.
Tony Hinton, First Assistant Secretary of Treasury's Investment and Debt Division, said that there would be a new 2010 benchmark issued in the second half of the fiscal year.
He also said that further issuance of the November 2006 line was unlikely.
Liquidity in this particular stock, which is still considered by some as the 10-year benchmark, has become fairly tight after the market's recent strong rally, traders said.
"A lot of the stock is held offshore, and the market always thinks it should be offered in a tender, but now it knows it won't be," one trader added.
The local market showed a modest outperformance against the dollar bloc and could put in a strong test on the 25 basis point spread differental to the U.S. if today's data proves weak.
U.S. Treasuries ended steady on Wednesday ahead of the final leg of the refunding auctions later on Thursday.
